title: AlphaFold-Designed De Novo Protein RF-409 Bypasses Defective Insulin Receptors In Vivo
aiSystem: AlphaFold 2.0 & Structure-Guided De Novo Protein Design
whyItMatters: An AI-designed single-chain protein sharing zero homology with insulin activated mutant insulin receptors in vivo, restoring glucose homeostasis in a mouse model of severe genetic insulin resistance.
summary: Published in Science Translational Medicine on November 25, 2026 by Albert Hung, Xinru Wang, Michael Gao, Domenico Accili, David Baker, and Eunhee Choi (Columbia University & University of Washington Institute for Protein Design), researchers engineered RF-409—a single-chain de novo polypeptide designed using AlphaFold 2.0 and computational protein engineering with no sequence or structural homology to human insulin. Two RF-409 molecules rigidly engage the insulin receptor extracellular domain at noncanonical sites to stabilize an active T-shaped dimer, bypassing pathogenic insulin-binding mutations (such as IR D707A seen in Donohue and Rabson-Mendenhall syndromes). In severe insulin-resistance mice where standard insulin fails completely, RF-409 restored glucose regulation, extended circulation half-life via albumin binding, and prevented pancreatic atrophy.
technicalHighlights: RF-409 shares zero sequence or structural homology with native two-chain insulin, instead using two rigidly α-helix-linked de novo domains to lock the receptor in its active conformation.
Activated patient-derived insulin-binding-deficient IR D707A mutant receptors in vivo—reversing hyperglycemia, hyperinsulinemia, lipoatrophy, and pancreatic atrophy where Humulin failed.
Exhibited markedly prolonged systemic circulation (via enhanced human serum albumin affinity) with broadly insulin-like phosphoproteomic signaling and no observed hepatic toxicity.
caveats: Validated in preclinical mouse models of severe insulin resistance; human immunogenicity, tissue-penetration kinetics, and long-term clinical safety remain to be evaluated in clinical trials.
institutions: University of Washington (Institute for Protein Design)

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrates that AI-designed noncanonical agonists can bypass genetic loss-of-function receptor mutations untreatable by natural hormones.
scoreRationale.ripple: Establishes a generalizable blueprint for engineering receptor-selective mimetics for severe receptoropathies, diabetes, and metabolic liver disease.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Science Translational Medicine with structural, phosphoproteomic, and in vivo preclinical efficacy data.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed de novo hormone-mimetic engineering from decades of peptide analog screening into targeted AI-guided structural design.
